subject: Help with Data Structure for a ggplot

messages.author: 26ed9ed356beb32b
messages.subject: Help with Data Structure for a ggplot
parts:
I'm attempting to use ggplot2 to make a several graphics to compare BMI to categorical variables such as Gender, Age, Family Income, Ratio of Family Income to Poverty etc.

The biggest hurdle I generally have when creating graphics is the issue of modeling the data before the graphics functions.

My goal with this is to be able to make a plot (Bar, or Line - I'll decide that when I actually write up the code for that) that compares the average BMI and one of the categorical variables, say Family Income. 

There are seven categories for Family Income and I'd like to find the mean BMI for each category of BMI and then plot that on a graph. I am having trouble with where to start when it comes to finding the mean BMI for each category. I hope once I get past this hurdle that I can then do this for the other categorical variables and create multiple graphics.

I've attached the output for dput(head(nh)) for my dataset:

> dput(head(nh))
structure(list(SeqN = c(51624L, 51628L, 51629L, 51630L, 51633L, 51635L), 
Gender = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L), 
Age = c(34L, 60L, 26L, 49L, 80L, 80L), 
Ethnicity = c(3L, 4L, 1L, 3L, 3L, 3L), 
FamSize = c(4L, 2L, 5L, 3L, 2L, 1L),
RatioIncomePoverty = c(1.36, 0.69, 1.01, 1.91, 1.27, 1.69), 
MECWgt2 = c(81528.77201, 21000.33872, 22633.58187, 74112.48684, 12381.11532, 22502.50666), 
BMI = c(32.22, 42.39, 32.61, 30.57, 26.04, 27.62),
LengthUS = c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_, NA_integer_, NA_integer_, NA_integer_, NA_integer_), 
Education = c(3L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 4L, 2L), 
LocationBorn = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), 
 FamIncome = c(6L, 3L, 6L, 7L, 4L, 4L)), 
.Names = c("SeqN", "Gender", "Age", "Ethnicity", "FamSize", "RatioIncomePoverty", "MECWgt2", "BMI", "LengthUS", "Education", "LocationBorn", "FamIncome"), row.names = c(NA, 6L), class = "data.frame")

A beginning direction for creating this mean BMI factor/variable for each categorical variable would definitely help and be appreciated. I haven't been able to figure out how to properly form a simple statement for what I am looking for in order to do a Google search.

Thank you.

parts:
And I actually figured part of it out.

nhh <-ddply(nh,.(FamIncome), summarise, mean.bmi=mean(BMI))

ethnicity is in the nh data set and the mean.bmi for Family Income is in the new dataset. I'd like to plot the mean.bmi for each factor of family income and have five lines showing the five different categorical ethnicities.
